title_en: Measures for the Administration of Toxic Drugs for Medical Use

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Measures are formulated in accordance with the provisions of the Drug Administration Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of strengthening the management of toxic drugs for medical use and preventing the occurrence of poisoning or death accidents.

Article 2 Toxic drugs for medical use (hereinafter referred to as toxic drugs) refer to drugs that are highly toxic, with a therapeutic dose close to a toxic dose, and may cause poisoning or death if improperly used.
The varieties of toxic drugs subject to administration shall be prescribed by the Ministry of Health jointly with the State Pharmaceutical Administration and the State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine.

Article 3 The annual plans for the production, purchase, supply and preparation of toxic drugs shall be formulated by the pharmaceutical administration departments of the provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government based on medical needs. After being examined and approved by the health administrative departments of the provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, the plans shall be issued by the pharmaceutical administration departments to the designated units for the production, purchase and supply of toxic drugs, and copies shall be submitted to the Ministry of Health, the State Pharmaceutical Administration and the State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine. Production units shall not change the production plans without authorization and sell the drugs on their own.

Article 4 Pharmaceutical factories shall assign medical professionals to be responsible for production, preparation and quality inspection, and shall establish a strict management system. They shall strictly prevent mixing with other drugs. Each batch of ingredients must be checked by at least two persons to ensure accuracy, and detailed records shall be kept of the raw materials and finished products used in each production. The persons handling the materials shall sign for future reference. All tools and containers shall be cleaned thoroughly to prevent contamination of other drugs. The labeled quantity shall be accurate, and the packaging containers shall bear a toxic drug mark.

Article 5 The purchase and operation of toxic drugs shall be undertaken by drug business units designated by the pharmaceutical administration departments at various levels; the dispensing of drugs shall be undertaken by state-owned pharmacies and medical units. No other unit or individual may engage in the purchase, operation or dispensing of toxic drugs.

Article 6 Units that purchase, operate, process or use toxic drugs must establish and improve systems for storage, acceptance, receipt and issue, and verification, shall strictly guard against accepting counterfeit drugs or issuing wrong drugs, and shall strictly prohibit mixing with other drugs. They shall designate specific warehouses or storage spaces, store the drugs in locked special cabinets, and assign special personnel for safekeeping.
The packaging containers of toxic drugs must bear a printed toxic drug mark. During the transportation of toxic drugs, effective measures shall be taken to prevent accidents.

Article 7 All processing and preparation of toxic traditional Chinese medicines must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Pharmacopoeia of the People's Republic of China or the Processing Specifications formulated by the health administrative departments of the provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government. The medicinal materials may only be supplied, dispensed, and used in the production of Chinese patent medicines if they meet the requirements for medicinal use.

Article 8 The production of toxic drugs and their preparations must strictly comply with the operation procedures of the production process, and raw materials shall be accurately fed under the supervision of the drug inspection personnel of the unit. Complete production records shall be established and kept for five years for future reference.
Waste generated during the production of toxic drugs must be properly disposed of and shall not pollute the environment.

Article 9 Medical units shall supply and dispense toxic drugs only upon a formal prescription signed by a doctor. State-owned pharmacies shall supply and dispense toxic drugs only upon a formal prescription bearing the official seal of the medical unit where the prescribing doctor works. The dosage per prescription shall not exceed the two-day maximum dose.
When dispensing a prescription, the personnel shall be conscientious and responsible, measure accurately, follow the instructions specified in the doctor's order, and the prescription may only be issued after being signed and sealed by the dispensing personnel and the checking personnel who hold a technical title of pharmacist or above. For toxic traditional Chinese medicines not marked with "crude use" on the prescription, the processed products shall be supplied. If any doubt arises regarding a prescription, it shall be re-dispensed only after re-examination and confirmation by the original prescribing doctor. Each prescription shall be valid for one use only. After the drugs are collected, the prescription shall be kept for two years for future reference.

Article 10 Toxic drugs required by scientific research and teaching units must be supplied and sold by the supply department only after the unit holds a letter of certification from its own unit and obtains approval from the health administrative department at or above the county level in the locality where the unit is located.
When the general public needs toxic traditional Chinese medicines for self-preparation of folk, secret, or empirical prescriptions, the supply department may sell them only after the purchaser presents a letter of certification from the purchaser's own unit or from the urban sub-district office or the people's government of the township (town). The quantity purchased each time shall not exceed the two-day maximum dose.

Article 11 Any unit or individual that violates the provisions of these Measures by producing, purchasing, or operating toxic drugs without authorization shall have all of their toxic drugs confiscated by the health administrative department at or above the county level, and shall be given a warning or imposed a fine of five to ten times the illegal income. If the circumstances are serious, causing disability or death, and constitute a crime, the judicial organ shall investigate criminal liability according to law.

Article 12 If a party is dissatisfied with the penalty, it may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the penalty notice, apply for reconsideration to the authority higher than the one that imposed the penalty. However, the original penalty decision shall still be executed during the period of reconsideration application. The higher authority shall make a reply within ten days from the date of receipt of the application. If the party is dissatisfied with the reply, it may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the reply, file a prosecution with the People's Court.
Article 13 These Measures shall be interpreted by the Ministry of Health.

Article 14 These Measures shall come into force as of the date of issuance. The Provisional Regulations on the Management of Toxic Drugs and Restricted Potent Drugs issued by the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Commerce, and the Ministry of Chemical Industry on April 20, 1964, the Interim Measures on the Management of Toxic Traditional Chinese Medicines issued by the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Commerce on December 7, 1964, and the Provisions on the Management of Toxic Drugs and Restricted Potent Drugs for Medical Use issued by the Ministry of Health and the State Pharmaceutical Administration on June 30, 1979 shall be abolished simultaneously.
